The Sovereign Harness — the Agentic

INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM
Series A2 | Prepared to support the Investment Committee evaluation of Further Ventures
August 2026
STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL — NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION
Prepared by AIREV Holding Limited (ADGM) for Further Ventures Limited solely to support Investment
Committee deliberations.

Further Ventures Limited solely to support Investment
Committee deliberations. This memorandum summarises signed commercial agreements at a level
consistent with AIREV’s confidentiality obligations to its counterparties; underlying agreements and the
company financial model are available in the data room under NDA. Financial projections are
management-prepared (base case) and unaudited.

1.  Executive summary
It took 2.5 years of R&D to build the sovereign harness. The product is the first moat, the factory pre-load
distribution is the second — and 2026 revenue is entirely platform licensing.

distribution is the second — and 2026 revenue is entirely platform licensing.
2.5 years of R&D built what does not otherwise exist in this region: OnDemand, a hybrid agentic AI
operating system — the sovereign harness — that runs on-device, on-premise, air-gapped or in cloud with
no cloud dependency, carrying 300+ pre-built agents, 3,000+ tools and ~97K verified users, certified SOC 2
Type I & II and ISO 27001:2022, and validated through engineering- and legal-grade diligence at Qualcomm,
Intel and Tenstorrent — all three signed.
Product-market fit is proven and paid for.

and Tenstorrent — all three signed.
Product-market fit is proven and paid for. Revenue moved from ~USD 1.0M of raw professional services in
year one to ~USD 1.2M of services delivered on the OnDemand platform in 2025 — including the
competitively won, fully delivered USD 250K Statement of Work for Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. (SOW
AIR-626951) — and steps up to USD 6.0M in 2026, all of it platform licensing revenue: per-device royalties,
enterprise licenses and perpetual licenses. The services era is over; it did its job.
Distribution is manufactured , not bought.

era is over; it did its job.

loaded across five silicon families at USD 100 per activated unit, perpetual; the signed Intel collaboration
carries the offline harness onto Intel AI PCs at the Panther Lake launch. The financial model has 111,000
devices carrying OnDemand by end-2026, compounding to ~1.05M by 2029.

T he ask is the model’s output, checked against the market. AIREV’s financial model prices Series A2
at USD 200M pre-money on a conservative 6.32x multiple of FY2029 contracted exit ARR, with a DCF cross-
check 15% higher at USD 229M — while agentic-AI peers fund at ~40–100x+ current ARR (LangChain USD
1.25B; n8n USD 2.5B; Sierra USD 10B; Glean USD 7.2B; Cognition USD 26B). At ~33x 2026 licensing revenue,
the entry sits ~45% below the peer median.
2.  Investment thesis: the sovereign harness
Models commoditise; the harness compounds.

thesis: the sovereign harness
Models commoditise; the harness compounds. The sovereign segment of the harness market has exactly
one purpose-built supplier between Europe and Asia — and it took 2.5 years to build.
Agent = Model + Harness . Enterprises do not deploy raw models; they deploy agents — a model wrapped in
orchestration, tools, data access, governance and audit. The harness holds the customer as models rotate
underneath it. OnDemand is that harness, packaged as an operating system.
Sovereignty is the wedge — and it cannot be retrofitted .

an operating system.
Sovereignty is the wedge — and it cannot be retrofitted . Government and regulated-enterprise buyers in
the GCC and the Global South require AI inside their perimeter. Cloud-first Western platforms would need
years of re-architecture to run air-gapped; OnDemand was engineered for it from day one — verified air-
gapped on the edge, validated on Intel Core Ultra, fully offline on AI PCs. The 2.5-year R&D lead is the entry
barrier.

Ultra, fully offline on AI PCs. The 2.5-year R&D lead is the entry
barrier.

The market is large and compounding: AI-agents market estimated at USD 7.84B in 2025, projected to USD
52.62B by 2030 at a 46.3% CAGR (MarketsandMarkets, 2025).
Timing: the UAE’s July 2026 move into US EAR Country Group A:5 eases approved access to advanced US
AI technology — and AIREV is already the agentic OS layer on Qualcomm-based sovereign infrastructure
programmes, with the silicon relationships signed.

5.  The first moat: the product
Silicon vendors do not sign perpetual licenses for slideware — the deepest diligence AIREV has faced was
run by Qualcomm’s, Intel’s and Tenstorrent’s own engineering and legal teams, and all three signed.
Code-level validation . The Qualcomm TLA grants QTI source-code scan rights (Open Source Review by
Qualcomm’s SAST and legal teams) with termination-and-refund remedies for non-compliance.

SAST and legal teams) with termination-and-refund remedies for non-compliance. Clearing that
bar — warranties on IP title, no restrictive code, privacy and third-party software — is itself a moat signal.
Hybrid + air-gapped capability peers lack . Cloud-first peers cannot serve air-gapped sovereign estates;
OnDemand’s hybrid engine is licensed, not roadmapped — written into the Qualcomm license scope and the
Intel deliverables.

7.2  Royalty unit economics

feasible.

8.  The second moat: distribution manufactured into the silicon
Software companies buy distribution customer by customer; AIREV manufactured it into the devices.
Displacing a factory pre-loaded OS requires re-manufacturing, not re-procurement.
OnDemand is not sold device-by-device — it ships inside them.

near-zero marginal cost. The signed Intel collaboration mirrors the motion on Intel AI PCs: a fully offline

market marketing exclusivity.

4. Edge Engineering Detail
“Your voice never leaves the device.”
STT and TTS execute completely on-edge on the Snapdragon AR1 Hexagon NPU, micro-NPU and
always-on audio path. There is no code path in the OnDemand AR1 runtime that transmits
microphone audio oﬀ the glasses — in either operating mode.
4.1 Speech pipeline on the AR1 audio path
Always-on wake word / low-power voice activation — runs on the AR1 low-power audio
subsystem, aligned with the platform's 'always-on audio' and wake-with- voice capabilities; the
main NPU stays asleep until the wake word is conﬁrmed.

voice capabilities; the
main NPU stays asleep until the wake word is conﬁrmed.
On-device streaming STT — a quantized streaming ASR model on the Hexagon NPU emits partial
transcripts within a few hundred milliseconds, with EN/AR support prioritised for the UAE launch
and additional locales added via OTA model packs.
On-device neural TTS — a compact neural vocoder pipeline renders speech to the custom
speakers with barge-in support so the wearer can interrupt the assistant.

speakers with barge-in support so the wearer can interrupt the assistant.
Audio hygiene — 5-mic beam-forming, echo cancellation for the open-ear speakers and a privacy
LED / HUD indicator whenever the microphones are active.
4.2 On-edge small language models
Two AIREV harness-tr ained SLMs serve local NLU, tool routing and conversational continuity (full
model cards in Section 6).

tool routing and conversational continuity (full
model cards in Section 6). The 0.8B model is the default on AR1 Gen 1-class memory budgets and
the always-res ident router on AR1+; the ~2B Gemma-4-E2B model is loaded on AR1+ for richer
oﬄine reasoning and plugin orchestration when thermal and battery headroom allow. Both emit
strict JSON tool calls, which is what makes a sub-1B model dependable as an on-glass agent.

tool calls, which is what makes a sub-1B model dependable as an on-glass agent.
4.3 Mini-RAG over private memory
A local retrieval layer indexes past interactions, documents, artifacts and explicit memories
(“remember where I parked”) into an on-device vector store. Retrieval happens before every SLM
turn, giving the oﬄine assistant continuity across days without any cloud account. Indexing is
deferred to charging or idle windows to protect battery, and the store lives inside the secure
enclave-backed encrypted partition.

and the store lives inside the secure
enclave-backed encrypted partition.

1. Executive summary A 50/50 joint venture with one mission in two parts: complete the 36-product agentic workforce for VVIP Sovereign JV partner first — then carry the same platform to the development ecosystem, cash-sustainable by design. The mission, in order. Part one — the primary mission — is supporting VVIP Sovereign JV partner: taking the 16 products already live to production grade and completing the roadmap of 36 products across the twelve departments, from Strategy and Humanitarian & Development Intelligence through Geopolitics & Policy, Foresight and Support Services.

Intelligence through Geopolitics & Policy, Foresight and Support Services. Part two extends the same platform and delivery muscle to the wider development ecosystem — the UAE Aid Agency, Erth Zayed Philanthropies, ADFD, the Emirates Red Crescent and the entities around them — the anchor cohort of ~500-seat contracting target. This is not a cold start. VVIP Sovereign JV partner brings a working analytical engine — 16 live products, nine functional skills, 25+ wired public data sources, 25 quantitative playbooks, 20+ slide builders, 437 files. AIREV brings OnDemand, the sovereign harness:

20+ slide builders, 437 files. The venture productises what already works. Delivery is forward-deployed, on signed rates.

productises what already works. Delivery is forward-deployed, on signed rates. Palantir-style FDE pods embed inside VVIP Sovereign JV partner and ecosystem entities, and build the agents, skills, connectors and orchestration — billed on the rate card from our signed MSA with ADQ, at a blended pod gross margin of ~48% (illustrative delivery margin before any arm’s-length related-party compensation to AIREV; JV-retained margin subject to the agreed terms). Not speculation: the rates are contractual. I nference is the viability question — so it has a rule-set.

are contractual. I nference is the viability question — so it has a rule-set. Closed frontier models are BYOI: the customer brings their own inference contract at their own risk, under a sovereignty disclaimer — assumed for ~50% of seats, so closed-model cost escalation never touches the venture.

2. The moment: the work is mandated, the tools do not fit, the engine already runs Three facts define the opportunity — and the venture is the only actor positioned at the intersection of all three. The push is national. The UAE National Strategy for AI requires every federal entity to adopt and scale AI, and the government has now announced that half of government services will run on AI agents within two years. The same pressure lands on the development sector: humanitarian, philanthropy and development bodies must show progress, on a trust bar higher than most.

and development bodies must show progress, on a trust bar higher than most. The market does not fit the work. Off-the-shelf tools miss development and humanitarian use cases; dataresidency and confidentiality needs go unmet; procurement is fragmented across entities, duplicating cost and inviting vendor lock-in; AI talent is scarce, so few entities can build and run their own; and no end-to-end player serves this ecosystem as a whole. Public data is abundant — and fragmented and underused. The engine already runs.

data is abundant — and fragmented and underused. The engine already runs. and internal audit in the huddles, an Erth Zayed curriculum in development. AIREV's harness — 2.5 years of R&D — is the platform layer this engine has been missing. United Arab Emirates ("AIREV") each a "Party" and together the "Parties". ARTICLE 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE 1.1 This Memorandum records the intention of the Parties to establish a jointly owned venture (the “Venture”) to develop and operate a sovereign, public-data-first artificial-intelligence capability serving the VVIP Sovereign JV partner and the United Arab Emirates development and humanitarian ecosystem, including the completion of the product roadmap developed within VVIP Sovereign JV partner and its extension to ecosystem entities.

within VVIP Sovereign JV partner and its extension to ecosystem entities. 1.2 Save for Articles 11 and 12, which the Parties intend to be binding upon signature, this Memorandum is a statement of intent and does not create legally enforceable obligations. Definitive terms shall be recorded in a Shareholders’ Agreement and associated documents, including a platform license agreement between AIREV and the Venture. ARTICLE 2 — FORMATION, OWNERSHIP AND CAPITALISATION 2.1 The Parties intend to incorporate the Venture in the United Arab Emirates as a limited liability company held in equal shares.

the United Arab Emirates as a limited liability company held in equal shares. 2.2 Each Party shall make a committed contribution of approximately [AED ●], matched in value and delivered predominantly in kind, which shall be valued and credited as equity so that the Parties hold equal shares. VVIP Sovereign JV partner’s contribution shall comprise seconded product owners, data subscriptions, the specialist adviser and office premises.

product owners, data subscriptions, the specialist adviser and office premises. AIREV’s contribution shall comprise seconded engineers, sovereign graphics-processing compute, platform hosting, cloud infrastructure, identity licensing, IT and shared services, and the platform license referred to in Article 6, which is contributed at nil value in accordance with Article 6.3. 2.3 Neither Party shall be required to subscribe cash equity.

with Article 6.3. 2.3 Neither Party shall be required to subscribe cash equity. Each Party shall keep callable cash of approximately [AED ●] so that the Venture remains solvent in at least [●] per cent of stress-tested scenarios, as agreed between the Parties. ARTICLE 3 — CONTRIBUTION OF PERSONNEL 3.1 Each Party shall second to the Venture, for the preparation period of approximately six (6) months leading to launch, not fewer than three (3) full-time equivalent personnel whose cumulative annual compensation cost is not less than AED 2,100,000.

whose cumulative annual compensation cost is not less than AED 2,100,000. The commitment is expressed as a value and a minimum headcount rather than a fixed rate per person, and where the fully-loaded cost of one Party’s personnel is lower than that of the other Party’s, that Party shall second additional personnel so that the value of the Parties’ commitments is matched.

additional personnel so that the value of the Parties’ commitments is matched. On the fully-loaded costs confirmed at the date of this Memorandum — AED 700,000 per VVIP Sovereign JV partner product owner and AED 420,000 per AIREV engineer — VVIP Sovereign JV partner shall second not fewer than three (3) product owners and AIREV not fewer than five (5) engineers. 3.2 VVIP Sovereign JV partner shall second product owners and AIREV shall second engineering personnel. Seconded personnel shall remain employees of, and on the payroll of, the seconding Party throughout the preparation period.

and on the payroll of, the seconding Party throughout the preparation period. The cost of seconded personnel shall form part of the seconding Party’s contribution under Article 2 and shall not be recharged to or reimbursed by the Venture. ARTICLE 4 — ALLOCATION OF OPERATING COSTS 4.1 Operating costs shall be borne according to which Party controls the decisions that drive them, and the obligations in this Article shall subsist for thirty-six (36) months from incorporation.

in this Article shall subsist for thirty-six (36) months from incorporation. 4.2 AIREV shall fund the sovereign compute on which the Venture’s own model pools run, together with platform hosting, cloud infrastructure and identity licensing. Consumption of third-party frontier models shall be procured and paid for by each consuming entity directly, and shall be an obligation of neither AIREV nor the Venture.

entity directly, and shall be an obligation of neither AIREV nor the Venture. 4.3 VVIP Sovereign JV partner shall fund data subscriptions, acquired progressively as the products relying upon them enter service, and external advisers, the specialist adviser being capped at [AED ●]. 4.4 AIREV shall provide IT and shared services, and VVIP Sovereign JV partner office premises, in kind for the first twenty-four (24) months; thereafter the Venture shall pay AIREV on a cost-plus basis and VVIP Sovereign JV partner a market rent.

pay AIREV on a cost-plus basis and VVIP Sovereign JV partner a market rent. All related-party transactions shall be valued at arm’s length in accordance with applicable United Arab Emirates transfer-pricing rules. ARTICLE 5 — DATA SUBSCRIPTIONS AND THIRD-PARTY LICENCES 5.1 All data subscriptions funded under Article 4 shall be contracted in the name of the Venture, so that negotiated rates, entitlements and vendor relationships vest in the Venture and survive any separation of the Parties.

relationships vest in the Venture and survive any separation of the Parties. 5.2 The Parties acknowledge that certain sources available without charge for non-commercial use require a commercial or public-sector licence once the Venture provides paid services, and that certain licences restrict redistribution, bulk retrieval or the creation of substitute datasets. The Venture shall maintain a licence register and obtain any required permission before an affected source is placed into production.

any required permission before an affected source is placed into production. ARTICLE 6 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PLATFORM LICENSE 6.1 Each Party shall retain ownership of the intellectual property it brings to the Venture — for VVIP Sovereign JV partner, the software tools, skills, methods, know-how and institutional content developed before the date of this Memorandum; for AIREV, the OnDemand platform, including its source code, harness architecture, routing and orchestration technology, connectors and deployment tooling — and shall license it to the Venture for the purposes of the Venture.

tooling — and shall license it to the Venture for the purposes of the Venture. 6.2 AIREV shall grant the Venture an operational license of the OnDemand platform, including the right to resell within the agreed field and territory, on the terms of a platform license agreement to be executed at or before incorporation. No license fee shall be payable by the Venture, the license forming part of AIREV’s contribution under Article 2. Any exclusivity within the field shall bind AIREV and shall not oblige the Venture or any ecosystem entity to use the platform.

and shall not oblige the Venture or any ecosystem entity to use the platform. AIREV shall provide platform-level support and release engineering to the Venture at documented cost with no uplift. 6.3 Background intellectual property shall be carried at nil value in the assessment of the Parties’ contributions and shall revert to and remain with its contributor. Intellectual property created by or for the Venture shall vest in the Venture.

Intellectual property created by or for the Venture shall vest in the Venture. 6.4 Upon any dissolution or separation, each Party shall receive a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence to use and commercialise the intellectual property created within the Venture, so that no valuation of that intellectual property is required in order to separate. No Party shall acquire rights in data belonging to a customer or ecosystem entity by reason of that data being processed by the Venture.

or ecosystem entity by reason of that data being processed by the Venture. 6.5 The VVIP Sovereign JV name and associated marks shall be registered in the name of, and held by, the Venture. ARTICLE 7 — FUNDING CEILING AND TRANSITION OF COST RESPONSIBILITY 7.1 AIREV shall fund the operating costs allocated to it under Article 4 up to a cumulative ceiling of [AED ●]. The costs falling within the ceiling shall be enumerated in a schedule to the Shareholders’ Agreement. Third-party frontier-model consumption and data subscriptions shall not fall within the ceiling.

consumption and data subscriptions shall not fall within the ceiling. 7.2 Responsibility for the enumerated costs shall pass to the Venture upon the later of exhaustion of the ceiling and expiry of the commitment period in Article 4. ARTICLE 8 — TRANSITION OF SECONDED PERSONNEL 8.1 Secondment serves the transfer of method and shall not constitute permanent staffing of the Venture.

transfer of method and shall not constitute permanent staffing of the Venture. Upon maturity of the product portfolio, personnel seconded by VVIP Sovereign JV partner shall step down and return to VVIP Sovereign JV partner, and the Venture shall recruit to its own payroll such personnel as are required to maintain the spans of control recorded in Article 9. Engineering personnel seconded by AIREV shall transfer to the employment of the Venture not later than six (6) months after incorporation, once the Venture’s employing entity, visa quota and payroll are established.

once the Venture’s employing entity, visa quota and payroll are established. The Venture shall employ its delivery personnel directly, and personnel engaged beyond the Parties’ committed contributions under Article 3 shall be employed by the Venture from the outset. 8.2 Each Party shall procure that its seconded personnel document their work so as to permit its continuation. ARTICLE 9 — QUALITY ASSURANCE AND SPANS OF CONTROL 9.1 Each product of the Venture shall have one named human owner accountable for its outputs.

of the Venture shall have one named human owner accountable for its outputs. During design an owner shall be responsible for not more than three products; once a product is mature, not more than four. 9.2 The Venture shall benchmark each product against recognised external sources before release and at intervals thereafter, and shall retain human approval at every gate at which its outputs become outputs of the government. ARTICLE 10 — SUBSCRIPTIONS, PRICING AND SURPLUS 10.1 The Venture shall be funded principally by committed subscriptions contracted with ecosystem entities.

principally by committed subscriptions contracted with ecosystem entities. Pricing shall be set so as to serve the ecosystem rather than to maximise return. 10.2 All revenue arising in the field, including subscriptions, platform licences, licence renewals, forward-deployed engineering and tenancy services, shall be contracted in the name of and booked by the Venture. 10.3 Any surplus shall be applied first to the reserves of the Venture and thereafter distributed in proportion to shareholdings. 10.4 The Venture shall maintain audited accounts and shall report to both shareholders quarterly.

maintain audited accounts and shall report to both shareholders quarterly. Each Party may present its attributable share of the Venture’s revenue and results in its own investor and group materials on a clearly labelled look-through basis, in accordance with applicable accounting standards. ARTICLE 11 — PORTABILITY, EXIT AND LIMITATION OF EXPOSURE (BINDING) 11.1 The products, skills and data connectors of the Venture shall be capable of operating upon any sovereign platform, and the Venture shall design its systems accordingly.

any sovereign platform, and the Venture shall design its systems accordingly. 11.2 Should either Party withdraw, the withdrawing Party shall be entitled to continue using the intellectual property it contributed, and the Venture shall retain the intellectual property created by it. 11.3 The exposure of each Party shall be limited to capital subscribed and contributions made or committed.

shall be limited to capital subscribed and contributions made or committed. ARTICLE 12 — TERM, CONFIDENTIALITY, EXCLUSIVITY AND COMPLIANCE (BINDING) 12.1 This Memorandum takes effect on signature and continues until the Shareholders’ Agreement is executed or either Party gives thirty (30) days’ written notice. 12.2 Each Party shall keep confidential the non-public information of the other Party, and shall use it only for the purposes of this Memorandum.

of the other Party, and shall use it only for the purposes of this Memorandum. 12.3 The Venture shall comply with the laws of the United Arab Emirates, including requirements relating to data residency and the protection of personal data. This Memorandum shall be governed by the laws of the United Arab Emirates.

This Memorandum shall be governed by the laws of the United Arab Emirates. 12.4 For ninety (90) days from the date of this Memorandum, extendable once by mutual written agreement, neither Party shall solicit, negotiate or conclude with any third party an arrangement substantially similar to the Venture within the United Arab Emirates development, humanitarian and philanthropic ecosystem (the “Field”). This undertaking is mutual and is limited to the Field.

(the “Field”). This undertaking is mutual and is limited to the Field. ARTICLE 13 — VALUATION AND VERIFICATION OF CONTRIBUTIONS 13.1 Contributions in kind shall be valued at arm’s length on a documented basis agreed between the Parties before incorporation, consistent with applicable United Arab Emirates transfer-pricing rules. Each Party shall deliver its contribution against an agreed delivery profile recording, for each component, the period of delivery and the value attributed to it.

for each component, the period of delivery and the value attributed to it. 13.2 Sovereign compute, platform hosting, cloud infrastructure and identity licensing shall be evidenced by supplier invoices or an auditable internal cost basis; seconded personnel by payroll records; data subscriptions and adviser fees by contract and invoice. 13.3 The Venture shall maintain a contribution register, reconciled semi-annually and reviewed by the Venture’s auditor.

register, reconciled semi-annually and reviewed by the Venture’s auditor. Any shortfall against the agreed profile shall be made good in cash or by further delivery within the following period, failing which the defaulting Party’s credited shareholding shall be adjusted accordingly. The register shall record the background intellectual property of both Parties at nil value in accordance with Article 6.3.

property of both Parties at nil value in accordance with Article 6.3. ARTICLE 14 — CHANGE OF PLATFORM DIRECTION 14.1 If VVIP Sovereign JV partner is directed by the VVIP Sovereign JV partner to adopt a system incompatible with the platform on which the Venture operates, VVIP Sovereign JV partner may elect either:

on which the Venture operates, VVIP Sovereign JV partner may elect either: (a) to deliver the balance of its committed contribution and retain its shareholding in full; or (b) to retain a shareholding proportionate to the value of the contribution it has delivered and verified to that date, forgo the balance, and continue as a passive investor without operational obligations. 14.2 In either case the licences granted under Article 6 shall survive, the Venture shall retain the data, tools and skills already contributed, and the portability undertakings in Article 11 shall continue to apply.

and the portability undertakings in Article 11 shall continue to apply. 14.3 VVIP Sovereign JV partner shall give not less than ninety (90) days’ written notice of an election under this Article, and the Parties shall meet within thirty (30) days of that notice to agree the consequential adjustments. ARTICLE 15 — GOVERNANCE 15.1 The board of the Venture shall comprise equal representation of the Parties, with an independent chair appointed by mutual consent. Neither any director nor the chair shall have a casting vote.

mutual consent. Neither any director nor the chair shall have a casting vote. 15.2 Funding for each wave of the product roadmap shall be released against the usage evidence agreed for the preceding wave. 15.3 The following matters shall require the consent of both Parties: (a) any change to the field, territory or term of the platform license; (b) compute capital decisions above a threshold to be agreed between the Parties, including the month-six owned-cluster decision; (c) related-party transactions;

including the month-six owned-cluster decision; (c) related-party transactions; (d) any use of government names, marks or insignia; and (e) the release of wave funding under Article 15.2. OnDemand Enterprise AI Orchestration Layer OnDemand is the world's first decentralized agentic AI operating system. Rather than relying on a single monolithic model to carry an entire workflow, OnDemand distributes intelligence across a coordinated network of specialized, lightweight agents that collaborate dynamically to deliver outcomes. The Agentic Mesh At the core of the OnDemand architecture is the Agentic Mesh.

The Agentic Mesh At the core of the OnDemand architecture is the Agentic Mesh. This decentralized network of specialized, lightweight agents communicates peer-to-peer, delegates tasks, and acts as an orchestration layer that makes raw intelligence actionable. By breaking complex business problems into discrete, agent-owned steps, the Agentic Mesh overcomes two structural limitations of traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) in enterprise environments: • Context Saturation : Complex, long-running enterprise tasks easily exceed a single model's usable context window.

enterprise tasks easily exceed a single model's usable context window. The Agentic Mesh partitions work across specialized agents so each operates within an optimal, highly focused context. • Latency and Cost in Workflows: Lightweight, purpose-built agents execute specialized functions faster and at a fraction of the cost of routing every trivial or intermediate step through a single monolithic frontier model. Enterprise Integrations & Unified Governance To operate as a true enterprise operating system, OnDemand features deep, native connectors into core enterprise systems of record.

Reporting & Success Metrics 8 11 Risk Management 9 12 Commercial Summary & Next Steps 9 SECTION 01 Executive Summary AIREV proposes a 24-month channel enablement program that establishes Redington as a fully equipped route to market for OnDemand, the decentralized agentic AI operating system.

route to market for OnDemand, the decentralized agentic AI operating system. The program provides four OnDemand base licenses as permanent, reusable demonstration infrastructure; two dedicated forward-deployed engineers; and a disciplined cadence of up to twelve managed client trial deployments — each delivered as a sealed, encrypted image and each running on an Intel-forward architecture. The commercial logic is deliberately simple. The four base licenses are never resold: they are Redington’s standing trial capability.

base licenses are never resold: they are Redington’s standing trial capability. Revenue compounds when trials convert — each converted client purchases its own OnDemand license, generating net-new, recurring revenue for Redington and AIREV beyond the initial program value of USD 500,000. The program is engineered for Intel’s current outcome-based Market Development Fund model.

is engineered for Intel’s current outcome-based Market Development Fund model. Every deployment is a pre-registered, Intel-architecture proof of concept with a measurable outcome — qualified enterprise pipeline and, where trials convert, closed Intel-silicon opportunities — supported by a complete, auditable evidence trail from registration to conversion. Program thesis Equip the channel once; convert repeatedly.

to conversion. Program thesis Equip the channel once; convert repeatedly. A permanent, engineer-supported trial capability inside Redington turns every qualified prospect into a structured, measurable, Intel-architecture opportunity — at a sustainable operating cadence of approximately one new client engagement per month. SECTION 02 Strategic Context This program brings together three complementary positions. Intel facilitated the introduction between AIREV and Redington, extending an existing technology relationship into a distribution motion.

extending an existing technology relationship into a distribution motion. Redington contributes enterprise reach and a mature Intel channel practice across the region. AIREV contributes the platform: OnDemand, a decentralized agentic AI operating system deployable across cloud, on-premises, edge, air-gapped and hybrid environments. OnDemand is validated on Intel architecture, with joint go-to-market activity that includes a co-published white paper on intel.com.

go-to-market activity that includes a co-published white paper on intel.com. The platform serves 97,000+ registered users, orchestrates 300+ AI agents across 3,000+ integrated tools, supports 50+ languages, and is SOC 2 and ISO certified. AIREV entered the UAE market through the Ministry of Economy’s NextGen FDI Programme and is headquartered in Abu Dhabi.

Ministry of Economy’s NextGen FDI Programme and is headquartered in Abu Dhabi. For Redington, the program converts distributor status into an active, differentiated sales motion: a supported, on-demand demonstration capability for agentic AI — a category enterprise and government buyers are actively procuring — anchored on the Intel silicon Redington already distributes. SECTION 03 Commercial Structure The program is a single commercial package with one purchase order and one program value. Components are not separately priced; together they constitute the enablement capability.

are not separately priced; together they constitute the enablement capability. Component | Specification Demonstration licenses | 4 × OnDemand base licenses, 32 seats each (128 seats in aggregate), 24-month term — permanent trial infrastructure, never resold Forward-deployed engineering | 2 dedicated AIREV forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) across the full term, supporting every deployment end to end Managed trial deployments | Up to 12 client deployments; each a sealed, encrypted OnDemand image run for 30 or 60 days at Redington’s discretion Enablement assets | Deployment playbooks, sales enablement, and the registration-to-conversion tracking framework (Section 06) Program governance | Monthly operating reviews, quarterly business reviews, and per-deployment evidence

operating reviews, quarterly business reviews, and per-deployment evidence packs supporting MDF claims Program value | USD 500,000 (twenty-four-month program) Commercial mechanics | Single purchase order issued by Redington to AIREV; invoicing and payment schedule to be confirmed in the definitive agreement SECTION 04 Program Sizing Rationale The program is sized around how trials actually run — not around a headline figure. Two settings work in deliberate tension: capacity to rotate, and discipline not to overrun. Four licenses — engineered for rotation Each deployment runs for 30 to 60 days.

Four licenses — engineered for rotation Each deployment runs for 30 to 60 days. Sustaining a cadence of approximately one new client per month across 24 months means multiple trials will routinely be live simultaneously — one concluding while the next two are already underway. Four base licenses provide the concurrency headroom to keep the pipeline in continuous motion, so no qualified prospect waits in a queue for a license to free up. Two licenses would force trials into strict sequence and bottleneck the program; four allow it to flow.

trials into strict sequence and bottleneck the program; four allow it to flow. A twelve-deployment cap — engineered for quality The cap is the counterweight to that headroom. Four licenses could technically support far more than twelve trials, but every deployment is backed by hands-on forward-deployed engineering — and the depth of that support is what converts trials into transactions.

— and the depth of that support is what converts trials into transactions. Capping the program at twelve deployments keeps engineering attention genuinely dedicated per client, protects delivery quality, and requires each trial slot to be allocated to a qualified, high-intent prospect rather than diffused across speculative activity. SECTION 05 Operating Model & Deployment Lifecycle Every engagement follows a six-stage lifecycle, jointly operated: Redington owns prospect qualification and the client relationship; AIREV owns technical delivery through the forward-deployed engineers.

AIREV owns technical delivery through the forward-deployed engineers. 01 Qualify | 02 Register | 03 Deploy | 04 Run | 05 Decide | 06 Convert Forward-deployed engineering scope. For each deployment, the FDEs deliver solution scoping against the client’s use cases, deployment of the sealed encrypted image into the client environment, integration and configuration, client enablement during the trial window, and structured support of the go/no-go decision. This is a managed engagement — not self-service trial software. Deployment format.

is a managed engagement — not self-service trial software. Deployment format. Each trial is provisioned as a sealed, encrypted OnDemand image. The moment the image goes live in the client environment constitutes formal registration of the deployment — a single, auditable timestamp from which the trial clock, the account-protection clock, the deployment-cap count and the Intel-architecture evidence record all run. SECTION 06 Trial-to-Conversion Framework The framework is a single, auditable pipeline keyed to one event: image-live registration.

is a single, auditable pipeline keyed to one event: image-live registration. One mechanism simultaneously serves the commercial agreement between AIREV and Redington and the evidentiary requirements of an outcome-based MDF claim. Stage 1 — Registration (trial start) On activation, every deployment is registered with the record below. The record is simultaneously the account-protection trigger and the Intel-architecture proof of performance.

the account-protection trigger and the Intel-architecture proof of performance. Registered field | Function Account (legal entity) | Triggers per-account exclusivity; prevents duplicate claims on the same account Deployment date (image live) | Starts the trial clock and the exclusivity clock; the auditable registration timestamp Trial length (30 / 60 days) | Sets trial expiry and the scheduled go/no-go date License assigned (1 of 4) | Tracks rotation and live concurrency across the demonstration licenses Deployment number (of 12) | Counts against the program cap Intel architecture confirmed | MDF-compliance flag evidencing the deployment ran on the Intel-forward stack Stage 2 — Trial active (30 / 60-day window) Engagement is tracked deliberately but lightly: named client stakeholders participating in the trial, use cases under evaluation, FDE touchpoints delivered, and a scheduled go/no-go decision date.

evaluation, FDE touchpoints delivered, and a scheduled go/no-go decision date. These signals evidence genuine client demand — the outcome class Intel’s current model is designed to fund — and provide the objective basis for releasing protection on any account that goes dormant. Stage 3 — Trial outcome At the go/no-go date, each deployment resolves to one of three states.

outcome At the go/no-go date, each deployment resolves to one of three states. Outcome | Definition | Consequence Converted | Client commits to OnDemand | Client issues its own license purchase order — net-new revenue and a closed Intel-silicon opportunity Qualified — open | Substantive interest; not yet closed | Recorded as a qualified lead — a fundable outcome under the outcome-based model; account enters protected nurture Closed — no conversion | No continuing opportunity | Exclusivity lapses at the six-month mark; the license slot returns to the rotation pool Stage 4 — Conversion tracking For every converted account, the program records licenses sold, purchase-order route, transaction value and close date.

records licenses sold, purchase-order route, transaction value and close date. This is the metric set that substantiates program return — the closed Intel-silicon opportunities anchoring the outcome-based MDF claim. SECTION 07 Account Protection To protect Redington’s investment of effort in developing each account, exclusivity is granted per account and triggered at registration. From the moment a trial is registered against a named legal entity, that account is exclusive to Redington for the duration of the trial plus six months following deployment.

Redington for the duration of the trial plus six months following deployment. Within that window, AIREV will not run a parallel trial or pursue a direct engagement with the same account through any other channel. Protection is earned, not blanket. It attaches only on formal registration of a trial against a specific named account — never pre-emptively across a target list — and an account showing no engagement activity for a sustained period may be released back into the general pipeline. Protected accounts therefore always correspond to genuine, active pursuit.

Protected accounts therefore always correspond to genuine, active pursuit. Design principle Registration is the contract. One timestamp — image live — starts the trial, starts the protection, counts the cap, and evidences the claim. There is nothing informal to dispute later. SECTION 08 Intel Technology Architecture OnDemand is architected so that Intel silicon runs the operating system itself. In every deployment, Intel Xeon is the compute backbone: orchestrating agents, executing the retrieval pipeline, generating embeddings, and running day-to-day agent models.

retrieval pipeline, generating embeddings, and running day-to-day agent models. Frontier-scale models are served by a dedicated accelerator layer — Intel Gaudi for a complete end-to-end Intel stack, or the client’s existing accelerator infrastructure where one is already in place. The footprint claim Intel silicon is present in 100% of OnDemand deployments as the platform layer — irrespective of which accelerator serves the largest models. This is a broader and more durable position than any single-workload claim.

This is a broader and more durable position than any single-workload claim. Where Intel runs — layer by layer OnDemand layer | Intel technology | Function Application & interface — Playground, Flow Builder, Web Chatbot, Collaborative Chat, Usage Dashboard | Intel Xeon | User sessions, interface logic, dashboards Agent orchestration — 300+ agents, multi-agent DAG flows, routing, conditional branching, parallel execution, human-in-the-loop | Intel Xeon | The operating-system core: scheduling and coordinating every agent and tool Tools & integration — 3,000+ tools, REST / webhooks, IoT / MQTT, MCP protocol | Intel Xeon | Tool execution, protocol handling, external integration Retrieval pipeline (RAG) — ingestion, chunking, vector pipeline management | Intel Xeon |

pipeline (RAG) — ingestion, chunking, vector pipeline management | Intel Xeon | Document parsing and pipeline orchestration Embeddings — document and image embedding generation | Intel Xeon + AMX via OpenVINO | Accelerated encoder inference (INT8 / BF16) Day-to-day agent models — BYOM ≤ 8B: routing, classification, summarization, tool-calling | Intel Xeon + AMX via IPEX-LLM / OpenVINO | On-CPU small-model inference for high-volume agent tasks Media services — transcription, text-to-speech, speech-to-text | Intel Xeon + AMX | Accelerated inference for compact media models Large / frontier model inference — complex reasoning models | Intel Gaudi (full-Intel stack) or existing accelerator via BYOI | Dedicated accelerator for the large-model forward pass Edge / AI PC —

BYOI | Dedicated accelerator for the large-model forward pass Edge / AI PC — on-device OnDemand runtime | Intel Core Ultra (CPU + NPU + iGPU) | On-device agent execution at the edge Intel software & optimization stack Platform performance on Intel is delivered through Intel’s own software stack: OpenVINO for accelerated embedding and small-model inference; Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX-LLM) for optimized language-model runtimes; and oneAPI as the unified programming layer across Xeon, Gaudi and Core Ultra.

and oneAPI as the unified programming layer across Xeon, Gaudi and Core Ultra. Embedding generation and sub-8-billion-parameter models are accelerated on Xeon through Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), Intel’s on-die matrix acceleration. Model routing Models that exceed the efficient envelope of CPU inference are routed through OnDemand’s model layer to a dedicated accelerator — Intel Gaudi where the client standardizes end to end on Intel, or the client’s existing accelerator estate via Bring-Your-Own-Inference.

or the client’s existing accelerator estate via Bring-Your-Own-Inference. In every configuration, Intel Xeon continues to run the full surrounding platform. For MDF-funded deployments, the demonstrated architecture is Intel-forward end to end. SECTION 09 Alignment with Intel’s Outcome-Based MDF Intel’s Market Development Fund model has moved from reimbursing marketing spend against receipts to funding pre-approved activities against demonstrated outcomes — qualified-lead generation foremost among them. The program is constructed to sit natively inside that model, on three principles.

program is constructed to sit natively inside that model, on three principles. Activity-based, outcome-tied. Each of the twelve deployments is a pre-registered, Intel-architecture proof of concept with a defined, measurable outcome: qualified leads, and — where trials convert — closed Intel-silicon opportunities. Under the outcome-based model, qualified leads constitute fundable results even ahead of transaction close. Intel architecture throughout.

results even ahead of transaction close. Intel architecture throughout. The demonstrated stack is Intel-forward end to end — Xeon running the platform, Intel’s optimization software delivering performance, and Intel Gaudi available for full-stack large-model inference — keeping every funded activity consistent with the Intel-architecture requirement. Reimbursement-aligned. The structure recognizes that MDF operates on a reimbursement basis against proven outcomes rather than upfront disbursement.

a reimbursement basis against proven outcomes rather than upfront disbursement. Program economics are therefore built around the registration-to-conversion evidence trail, which substantiates each funded activity as executed. Approval pathway MDF activity is treated as approved only upon issuance of a formal project identifier through Intel’s marketing exchange. This program is designed to be submitted for that pre-approval as an Intel-architecture lead-generation initiative, with the per-deployment evidence pack prepared to support each claim.

with the per-deployment evidence pack prepared to support each claim. SECTION 10 Governance, Reporting & Success Metrics The program operates under a light but formal governance rhythm, designed to keep delivery on cadence and to produce claim-ready evidence as a by-product of normal operation.

and to produce claim-ready evidence as a by-product of normal operation. Forum / instrument | Purpose & cadence Monthly operating review | AIREV + Redington: pipeline of qualified prospects, live deployments, license rotation, FDE allocation, upcoming go/no-go decisions Quarterly business review | AIREV + Redington + Intel stakeholder: outcomes against plan, MDF claim status, pipeline value, conversion performance Per-deployment evidence pack | Registration record, engagement log, outcome classification, and — where converted — purchase-order confirmation; assembled per deployment to support the MDF claim Success metrics Formal targets are baselined jointly at program kickoff.

claim Success metrics Formal targets are baselined jointly at program kickoff. The measurement set is fixed from day one. Metric | Definition Deployments activated | Registered deployments against the cap of twelve Trial completion rate | Trials reaching a formal go/no-go decision as a share of trials started Qualified leads generated | Accounts resolving to Converted or Qualified — open Trial-to-conversion rate | Converted accounts as a share of completed trials (planning basis:

rate | Converted accounts as a share of completed trials (planning basis: 25–35%) Net-new license revenue | Value of OnDemand licenses purchased by converted clients Intel-silicon opportunities closed | Converted deployments delivered on the Intel-forward architecture — by design, all of them SECTION 11 Risk Management Principal delivery risks are addressed structurally within the program design rather than managed reactively. Risk | Structural mitigation Over-subscription of engineering capacity | Hard cap of twelve deployments;

Over-subscription of engineering capacity | Hard cap of twelve deployments; FDE allocation reviewed monthly; trial slots reserved for qualified, high-intent prospects Dormant protected accounts | Exclusivity attaches only on formal registration; sustained inactivity triggers release of the account back to the general pipeline MDF approval timing | No activity is treated as funded before a formal project identifier is issued; program economics do not depend on prepayment Architecture compliance | Intel-architecture confirmation is a mandatory registration field; every deployment carries its own compliance evidence SECTION 12 Commercial Summary & Next Steps USD 500,000 secures a 24-month, engineer-supported channel capability: four permanent demonstration licenses, twelve managed Intel-architecture client deployments, dedicated forward-deployed engineering, per-account protection, and a claim-ready evidence framework.

engineering, per-account protection, and a claim-ready evidence framework. Every conversion generates net-new license revenue beyond the program itself — and every converted deployment is, by design, an Intel-silicon opportunity. Next steps Redington & Intel — submit the program for MDF pre-approval as an Intel-architecture lead-generation initiative and secure the formal project identifier. AIREV — on approval, allocate the two forward-deployed engineers and provision the four base licenses as standing trial infrastructure.

and provision the four base licenses as standing trial infrastructure. Joint — finalize the account-registration process and confirm exclusivity, conversion and invoicing terms in the definitive channel agreement. Leadership is invited to endorse the ranked portfolio, confirm lead owners, and commission a 90-day implementation design. المطلوب / Requested: Kind approval to (1) adopt the three ranked priorities below as the five-year diversification focus;

adopt the three ranked priorities below as the five-year diversification focus; (2) designate the named lead entities; and (3) direct a cross-entity delivery unit to return within 90 days with initiative charters, KPIs and budget envelopes for 2026–2028. الخلفية — PROBLEM DEFINITION AND CONTEXT Abu Dhabi’s long-term strategy aims to reduce reliance on oil as the dominant source of economic activity and build a knowledge-based, globally integrated economy. The Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030 (Government of Abu Dhabi;

economy. The Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030 (Government of Abu Dhabi; UAE Government portal, updated 30 Dec 2024) prioritises an open business environment, labour-market efficiency, infrastructure resilience, a highly skilled workforce, and financial markets that finance productive sectors. At federal level, UAE Centennial 2071 frames multi-decade ambition on future skills and soft power; the updated UAE Energy Strategy 2050 (u.ae) targets a sharp rise in clean energy and cites investment on the order of AED 150–200 billion by 2030; ADNOC’s public strategy centres on “Maximum Energy.

150–200 billion by 2030; ADNOC’s public strategy centres on “Maximum Energy. Minimum Emissions,” pairing competitive hydrocarbon supply with decarbonisation (ADNOC, 2025–2026). Why 2026–2031 matters. This window is the decisive stretch of Vision 2030 and the first full delivery cycle after the post-pandemic rebound. Macro data show a larger, more investable economy — but manufacturing depth and R&D intensity remain below structural peers, while resource rents still move with the oil cycle.

below structural peers, while resource rents still move with the oil cycle. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Analysis Analysis and prioritisation CRITERIA Candidate priorities scored against six criteria: (1) impact on non-oil GDP; (2) feasibility in five years; (3) alignment with existing strategies; (4) job creation; (5) FDI attraction; (6) resilience. OPTION SET SCREENED Advanced manufacturing; AI/digital/knowledge services; clean energy value chains; tourism/culture; logistics/trade; financial services deepening; agritech; space/advanced mobility.

financial services deepening; agritech; space/advanced mobility. Tourism, culture and logistics remain important enablers but do not clear the top-three bar on the combined criteria relative to the three below. RANKING RATIONALE Rank Priority Why it clears the bar Advanced industry and manufacturing depth Largest structural gap vs peers (mfg ~9% GDP); multiplies non-oil GDP and export complexity; Vision 2030 alignment; FDI can be steered into plants. Knowledge economy:

Vision 2030 alignment; FDI can be steered into plants. Knowledge economy: AI, digital infrastructure and high-value services Highest jobs-and-FDI multiplier in five years; services already >half of GDP — upgrading composition matters; Centennial 2071 human-capital alignment. Clean energy and energy-transition value chains Converts hydrocarbon advantage into transition-era resilience; Energy Strategy 2050 and ADNOC rails ready; renewable share still low — large build opportunity. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026·2031 Internal · Senior Decision-Makers VVIP Sovereign JV partner

Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Priority 1 Priority 1 — Advanced industry and manufacturing depth RANK 1 Build a thicker, higher-complexity industrial base in Abu Dhabi by 2031 Rationale. Manufacturing VA remains about 9.4% of UAE GDP (2024), versus ~15.8% in Saudi Arabia and ~17.4% in Singapore (World Bank WDI). Industry overall is large (~44% of GDP) because it includes oil and gas; the diversification problem is the thin manufacturing slice. Closing part of the peer gap over five years is among the highest-leverage non-oil GDP moves available.

gap over five years is among the highest-leverage non-oil GDP moves available. It also raises export sophistication (high-tech share of manufactured exports ~9% in 2023). Strategic alignment. Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030; federal industrial and advanced-technology agendas; Abu Dhabi industrial and investment programmes. Expected outcomes (2026–2031). Rise in manufacturing VA share and non-oil industrial GVA; 3–5 anchor greenfield or major expansion projects in priority verticals; higher local content in energy and construction supply chains; several thousand skilled technical roles.

and construction supply chains; several thousand skilled technical roles. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Priority 2 Priority 2 — Knowledge economy: AI, digital and high-value services RANK 2 Shift services composition toward AI, digital, professional and financial services that export and stick Rationale. Services already contribute about 55% of UAE GDP (2024). Diversification is not “more services” in the abstract — it is higher-value, tradable knowledge services and the digital infrastructure that makes Abu Dhabi a preferred base. FDI inflows reached US$ 45.6 B in 2024 (WDI), a rare window to convert capital attraction into capability attraction.

(WDI), a rare window to convert capital attraction into capability attraction. R&D intensity rose to ~1.5% of GDP (2021) from 0.47% in 2011, but remains well below innovation leaders. Strategic alignment. UAE Centennial 2071; Vision 2030 business-environment and human-capital pillars; Abu Dhabi technology and startup ecosystem (e.g. Hub71 and related platforms, ADMO economy coverage, 2026). Expected outcomes (2026–2031).

related platforms, ADMO economy coverage, 2026). Expected outcomes (2026–2031). Growth in ICT and professional-services GVA; scale-up employment; more regional HQs and product-engineering centres; higher applied R&D; stronger Emirati participation in tech and advanced services. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Priority 3 Priority 3 — Clean energy and energy-transition value chains RANK 3 Turn energy advantage into a transition-era industrial and investment platform Rationale. Resource rents still accounted for about 17.6% of UAE GDP in 2021 and fluctuate with the cycle (WDI). Resilience requires competitive energy supply and clean power, lower-carbon molecules, and transition equipment/services that generate non-oil value added. Updated UAE Energy Strategy 2050 aims to triple renewable contribution and cites AED 150–200 billion by 2030 (u.ae).

to triple renewable contribution and cites AED 150–200 billion by 2030 (u.ae). Renewable electricity was only about 4.2% of output in 2021 (WDI) — a large execution gap and build opportunity. ADNOC places decarbonisation at the centre of growth strategy. Strategic alignment. UAE Energy Strategy 2050; national net-zero direction; ADNOC sustainability strategy; Vision 2030; Masdar and related clean-energy platforms. Expected outcomes (2026–2031).

2030; Masdar and related clean-energy platforms. Expected outcomes (2026–2031). Material increase in clean power capacity and local content of transition projects; growth of non-oil energy-services and equipment activity; stronger climate-aligned FDI; reduced long-run concentration risk. Power, land and water as industrial policy tools — published packages for priority projects. Skills compact linking education entities to the three priority labour markets. الاعتبارات — CONSIDERATIONS Why not rank tourism/culture or logistics first? Both remain active portfolio elements. They score lower than the top three on the combination of structural non-oil GDP depth, transition resilience, and ability to absorb the FDI surge into tradable capability. Federal vs emirate instruments. Several statistics and strategies are federal; delivery is highly emirate-shaped in Abu Dhabi. Recommendation: an Abu Dhabi portfolio that rides federal rails. an Abu Dhabi portfolio that rides federal rails. Evidence limits. Emirate-disaggregated manufacturing VA and FDI-by-sector series are not fully available in WDI/IMF extracts. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Talking Points الحديث نقاط — Talking Points (≈5 minutes) 1. Open with the ask. Lock three diversification priorities for 2026–2031 — advanced industry, knowledge/AI services, and clean-energy value chains — and return in 90 days with owners, KPIs and budgets. 2. The economy is larger and more investable. UAE GDP reached about US$ 552 billion in 2024; FDI inflows about US$ 46 billion. Convert this into productive capacity, not only capital inflows. (World Bank WDI) 3. The structural gap is manufacturing depth.

capital inflows. (World Bank WDI) 3. The structural gap is manufacturing depth. Manufacturing is still roughly 9% of GDP, well below Saudi Arabia and Singapore. Industry looks large only because oil sits inside it. That is Priority One. 4. Services must upgrade, not just expand. Services are already over half of GDP. Priority Two is AI, digital infrastructure and exportable professional services — while R&D intensity, improved to ~1.5% of GDP, must keep rising with application. 5. Transition is resilience, not charity.

must keep rising with application. 5. Transition is resilience, not charity. Resource rents remain material; renewable electricity was only about 4% of output in 2021 against Energy Strategy 2050 ambition. Priority Three turns energy advantage into clean power, transition industry and finance. 6. Main risk: strategy proliferation without FIDs. Discipline = capped initiative list, single scorecard, quarterly kill-orscale. 7. Close on governance. Endorse the ranking, name sponsors, stand up the delivery unit, require the 90-day charter pack. 8.

name sponsors, stand up the delivery unit, require the 90-day charter pack. 8. [الوقت سمح إذا / if time permits] Peer chart: manufacturing VA — UAE ~9%, Saudi ~16%, Singapore ~17%, Korea ~27%. Economic Diversification Priorities 2026·2031 Internal · Senior Decision-Makers VVIP Sovereign JV partner

Economic Diversification Priorities 2026–2031 · Q&A متوقعة أسئلة — Anticipated Questions & Answers Q1. Why only three priorities — will we neglect tourism, logistics and culture? Suggested response: No. Those sectors remain active portfolio elements and demand generators. The three priorities best combine non-oil GDP depth, five-year feasibility, FDI conversion and energy-transition resilience. If pressed: Keep a monitored tier-two list, but do not split leadership bandwidth equally across ten themes. Q2. Oil prices are supportive — why accelerate diversification now? Suggested response:

prices are supportive — why accelerate diversification now? Suggested response: Supportive prices are when we can fund the transition without stress. Resource rents still moved between roughly 12% and 18% of GDP in recent WDI observations. Waiting for a down-cycle raises adjustment costs. Q3. What is the budget ask? Suggested response: No single envelope today. Authority is sought to return in 90 days with initiative-level envelopes for 2026–2028, distinguishing public catalytic spend, regulated offtake, and mobilised private/FDI capital.

public catalytic spend, regulated offtake, and mobilised private/FDI capital. Energy Strategy 2050 already signals federal-scale clean-energy investment needs of AED 150–200 billion by 2030 — Priority 3 will map the Abu Dhabi share of bankable projects. If pressed: No open-ended funding; every initiative will carry unit costs, milestones and kill criteria. Q4. How does this differ from existing strategies (Vision 2030, industrial programmes)? Suggested response: It does not replace them. It concentrates them. The gap has been diffusion of effort.

not replace them. It concentrates them. The gap has been diffusion of effort. This portfolio picks the three highest-yield execution themes for five years and attaches owners, timeframes and enablers. Q5. Why is manufacturing ranked above clean energy if the transition is existential? Suggested response: Clean energy is Priority Three, not optional. locally relevant AI. The funder's own language is the sovereignty pitch. card, so one ~160kW box serves tens of thousands of concurrent learners . The Platform · Four Sectors 08 Same infrastructure. Four national-priority sectors.
